data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Safety is the strictly stronger property and the one the log must require. In the retry/RPC literature, 'safety' means an operation may be repeated without any observable additional effect \u2014 not merely that the final state converges, but that no intermediate state, side effect, or external observable differs between one execution and n executions. Idempotency is weaker: it only guarantees f(f(x))=f(x) at the level of the operation's return value or final state, saying nothing about harmful intermediate states or external side effects during the duplicate execution. An idempotent operation that temporarily deletes and re-inserts a log entry during its second execution would leave the same final state but could corrupt a concurrent reader \u2014 it is idempotent but not safe. The append-only log must require safety because at-least-once delivery means retries happen in a live system where intermediate states are observable.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log is single-threaded with no concurrent observers during retry, intermediate states are unobservable and safety's extra guarantee is vacuous \u2014 pure idempotency suffices.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'safety' is defined merely as 'does not crash or corrupt' (a weaker notion), then it does not subsume idempotency and the claim that it is strictly stronger fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the published definition of safety referenced by the problem is the distributed-systems safety/liveness distinction ('bad things never happen' vs 'good things eventually happen'), then safety is about protocol invariants, not retry behavior, and the claim conflates two different uses of 'safe.'","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under at-least-once delivery, the retry of a write operation occurs while the system may be actively serving reads or further writes. An idempotent-but-unsafe operation could produce a transient inconsistency (e.g., momentarily removing a prior entry, then re-adding it) that is visible to concurrent operations. A safe operation guarantees that the retry is indistinguishable from no-retry at every observable point, not just at the final state. Thus safety \u2261 idempotency + no-harmful-intermediate-states, making safety the property the log must enforce.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
